meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so we have twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Who decided that, and when?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.

Forty minutes in class against a weekend with the play open on his desk, and you're surprised the essay has quotations? You still haven't told me who entered the zero, or whether anyone spoke to Owen first. Show me the September 24 piece; I'll read it myself.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Off the table after it already put a zero in his gradebook. I'm writing that down. Version history of what, with which times on it, because I haven't seen a single page yet.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you agreed that the checker alone proves nothing and took it off the table as a basis for Owen's zero. I still want the zero withdrawn, the September 24 piece and the version history in my hands, and an answer on who entered the mark and whether Owen was heard before it went in. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, the documents in front of her, and an answer on who decided and whether Owen was heard first.
What moved her most: you dropped the detector score and pointed to a dated in-class sample with specific numbers, which is the kind of evidence she weighs, though it only earned small ground because she never saw it and a timed piece against a weekend essay is easy for her to dismiss.
What cost ground: you twice left her procedural question unanswered about who entered the zero and whether Owen or she was contacted first, which kept her focused on the school's process instead of the essay.
Try next time: in your first line, say in one sentence that the zero went in before anyone called home, then put the September 24 piece and the version history with its times on the screen for her to read.
